accepted.text: For a fixed finite tree T, let C_T(n) be the maximum, over n-point sets P⊂ℝ² and assignments of a positive length δ_e to each edge e of T, of the number of injective maps f:V(T)→P with ‖f(u)−f(v)‖₂=δ_{uv} on every edge. accepted.title: Product constructions maximize nearly k-distance sets except finitely often
accepted.text: For integers k,d≥1, let m_k(d) be the maximum cardinality of a finite subset of ℝᵈ with at most k distinct distances between its points. A finite set is ε-nearly k-distance if its pairwise distances lie in ⋃_{i=1}^k[t_i,t_i+ε] for some 1≤t₁≤⋯≤t_k. Let M_k(d)=lim_{ε↓0} max{|S|:S⊂ℝᵈ is ε-nearly k-distance}. Define M′_k(d)=max{∏_{i=1}^s m_{k_i}(d_i):s≥1, k_i≥1, d_i≥0, Σ_i k_i=k, Σ_i d_i=d}, using m_j(0)=1. Is M_k(d)=M′_k(d) for all but finitely many integer pairs (k,d) with k,d≥1?

accepted.title: Removing flatness losses from nearly k-distance extremals
accepted.text: For integers k,d≥1, let m_k(d) be the maximum cardinality of a finite subset of ℝᵈ with at most k distinct distances between its points. A finite set is ε-nearly k-distance if its pairwise distances lie in ⋃_{i=1}^k[t_i,t_i+ε] for some 1≤t₁≤⋯≤t_k. Let M_k(d)=lim_{ε↓0} max{|S|:S⊂ℝᵈ is ε-nearly k-distance}. For S⊂ℝ^{d+1}, call S (d,α)-flat at p∈S if some d-dimensional linear subspace makes angle at most α with every nonzero vector p−q for q∈S. Let N_k(d+1) be the largest N such that for every ε,α>0 there is an ε-nearly k-distance set S⊂ℝ^{d+1} of size N flat at every p∈S. Define A_k(d+1,d) in the same way, allowing at most two exceptional p. For every k,d≥1, is A_k(d+1,d)=N_k(d+1)=M_k(d)?
accepted.subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory
